assumptions: Entry signals are evaluated after each closed M15 candle; H1 candles are admitted only after their modeled close time.
Historical news is unavailable. The primary news-neutral score assumes riskScore 0; a parallel scenario assumes UNAVAILABLE with riskScore 60.
Signals are counted at every eligible candle. Only one pending/open order per pair is simulated at a time, without score-based rejection.
Limit entry is the planned entry-zone midpoint, active for the next 8 M15 bars; unfilled orders expire.
After fill, TP2 is the target and SL the stop; maximum hold is 32 M15 bars. Same-bar stop/target ambiguity is resolved as a stop first.
Spread and slippage are unavailable. Expectancy is shown at 0R, 0.05R, and 0.10R round-trip friction per trade.
Drawdown is sequential closed-trade drawdown in R for this one-position simulation, not a broker-equity forecast.
The first 70% of M15 history is the calibration period; the final 30% is a chronological holdout. No weights or thresholds were fitted on the holdout.
The replay uses the latest provider history returned for each request; actual history length can be shorter than requested and this is not a tick-level execution simulation.
The final 40 M15 bars of each split are excluded as signal times so pending entries and the maximum holding window finish inside their own period.
Provider timestamps have no explicit timezone in the candle rows; calculations assume H1 and M15 use the same provider timezone and reports retain the original timestamp strings.

findings: News-neutral out-of-sample score band 0-39: 278 trades, 25.2% win rate, -0.290R expectancy after assumed 0.05R friction.
News-neutral out-of-sample score band 40-59: 113 trades, 34.5% win rate, 0.013R expectancy after assumed 0.05R friction.
News-neutral out-of-sample score band 60-79: 31 trades, 35.5% win rate, 0.109R expectancy after assumed 0.05R friction.
News-neutral out-of-sample score band 80-100: 5 trades, 20.0% win rate, -0.450R expectancy after assumed 0.05R friction.
These results are a short-window replay, not proof of future profitability or a calibrated win probability; preserve the per-pair drawdowns and sample counts when interpreting aggregate bands.
The current Risk Reward checklist uses TP2, which is constructed at 2R from planned entry; its 5-point score contribution is therefore not an independent reward-quality measurement.
No score weights, thresholds, or setup gates were changed during this validation, so the holdout remains untouched.
limitations: Historical news is not archived by the configured headline/calendar sources, so results include news-neutral and news-unavailable score scenarios rather than reconstructed historical news.
The provider returns a rolling history window; M15 coverage determines the effective replay horizon.
OHLC data cannot model exact intrabar sequence, bid/ask spread, queue position, or real slippage.
